verdicts.reasoning: The source recipe marinates the pork overnight in 1/2 cup Walker's Wood jerk seasoning before slow cooking - this is the sole flavor source for the dish and our list has zero seasoning of any kind.

Slender Kitchen explicitly states 'the key to this dish is the sauce...made with a combination of soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, red onion, ginger, rice vinegar, and jalapenos' - rice vinegar is a named core sauce component that is completely absent from our list, unlike the jalapeno/heat element which the recipe itself calls optional/substitutable.

Skinnytaste's recipe (soy sauce, apple cider vinegar, garlic, peppercorns, 4-6 bay leaves) uses bay leaf as a defining aromatic alongside soy+vinegar+garlic - real adobo is standardly soy sauce + vinegar + garlic + bay leaf, and bay leaf is missing entirely from our list while soy sauce/vinegar/garlic/onion are already present.

The Real Food Dietitians recipe lists 1/2 teaspoon dried oregano as a distinct seasoning alongside cumin (3/4 tsp) - oregano is a standard defining spice in Cuban-style picadillo and is completely absent from our stored list, which only has cumin as its spice.
